common_name: Siloam Jandee Daylily (Gold Eyezone Miniature Siloam Series)

planting.note: Plant dormant-foliage divisions in spring or early fall in well-drained soil in full sun; this compact diploid Siloam-series introduction forms a tidy clump and multiplies readily once established.

directions: A fragrant, dwarf-statured member of the Siloam series bred by Pauline Henry, this diploid daylily bears gold flowers marked with a red-brown eyezone above a green throat on compact scapes barely over a foot tall. Blooms open in an early-to-midseason flush with an extended habit, keeping individual flowers open longer in the day than typical for the genus. Grow in full sun in average, well-drained soil and divide congested clumps every few years in spring to sustain heavy bloom on this small-flowered, front-of-border type.

common_name: Siloam Flower Girl Daylily (Rose Eyezone Dwarf Siloam Series)

planting.note: Plant dormant-foliage divisions in spring or early fall in well-drained soil in full sun; this dwarf diploid Siloam-series daylily forms a dense, grassy clump that bulks up quickly once established.

directions: Bred by Pauline Henry, this fragrant diploid Siloam-series daylily bears rose-pink flowers accented by a red eyezone and a green throat, carried on scapes under two feet tall. It blooms in an early-to-midseason flush with an extended-bloom habit that keeps each flower open later in the day than most daylilies. The small, dormant-foliage clump is well suited to the front of a mixed border and benefits from division every three to four years to maintain a high bud count.

common_name: Siloam Springs Daylily (Soft Yellow Early Siloam Series)

planting.note: Plant dormant-foliage divisions in spring or early fall in well-drained soil in full sun; this early diploid Siloam-series introduction forms a vigorous clump that multiplies steadily once established.

directions: One of Pauline Henry's first registered daylilies and named for her hometown of Siloam Springs, Arkansas, this fragrant diploid bears a soft yellow self-colored flower with a faint green throat on scapes near three feet tall. It opens in a heavy midseason flush with an extended-bloom habit, and its dormant foliage dies back fully each winter before vigorous spring regrowth. Grow in full sun in average, well-drained soil and divide congested clumps every three to four years to keep bloom production strong.

common_name: Siloam Mama Daylily (Yellow Self Siloam Series)

planting.note: Plant dormant-foliage divisions in spring or early fall in well-drained soil in full sun; this diploid Siloam-series daylily forms a full, rounded clump that increases readily once established.

directions: Bred by Pauline Henry, this fragrant diploid Siloam-series daylily carries a clear yellow self-colored flower with a green throat on two-foot scapes, opening in an early-to-midseason flush with an extended-bloom habit. The large, single blooms sit atop a dormant-foliage clump that dies back cleanly in winter and bulks up vigorously the following growing season. Grow in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil and divide every three to four years to sustain heavy flowering.

common_name: Siloam Queens Toy Daylily (Pink Halo Miniature Siloam Series)

planting.note: Plant dormant-foliage divisions in spring or early fall in well-drained soil in full sun; this compact diploid Siloam-series miniature forms a dense, grassy clump that increases steadily once established.

directions: A miniature-flowered diploid from the Siloam series bred by Pauline Henry, this daylily bears pale pink blooms ringed with a deeper pink halo above a green throat, carried on scapes under two feet tall. It flowers in a midseason flush with an extended-bloom habit, holding each small, crisp bloom open longer into the day than many larger-flowered cultivars. The dormant-foliage clump suits edging or small-space plantings and divides easily every few years to keep bud counts high.

common_name: Siloam Red Ruby Daylily (Compact Red Self Siloam Series)

planting.note: Plant dormant-foliage divisions in spring or early fall in well-drained soil in full sun; this compact diploid Siloam-series daylily forms a tidy, small-flowered clump that multiplies readily once established.

directions: Bred by Pauline Henry, this diploid Siloam-series daylily bears a clear red self-colored flower with a green throat on scapes around a foot and a half tall, giving a saturated pop of color from a compact, dormant-foliage clump. It opens in a midseason flush with an extended-bloom habit, and its small flower size and low stature suit the front of a border or massed plantings. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to keep flower counts high.

common_name: Jedi Blue Note Daylily (Lavender-Blue Semi-Evergreen Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; this semi-evergreen diploid from the Jedi series establishes quickly and multiplies readily once rooted in.

directions: Part of the Jedi series of daylilies bred by Wedgeworth, this lightly fragrant diploid bears large, lavender-blue flowers with a green throat on scapes under two feet tall, opening in a diurnal, early-to-midseason display. The semi-evergreen foliage holds up through mild winters better than fully dormant daylilies, though it can be damaged in harder freezes. Grow in full sun to light afternoon shade in average, well-drained soil and divide congested clumps every three to four years to sustain vigorous flowering.
